$comment: Conditional branches (`then`, and a `not` inside one) that require a property also declare it as `"properties": { "<name>": true }`. That is deliberately not a constraint - a boolean `true` schema permits anything. It exists because the validator runs Ajv with `strict: true`, and Ajv's `strictRequired` rule rejects a `required` entry whose property is not declared in that same subschema object. Keeping the branch self-contained satisfies the rule without changing its meaning; the valid and invalid fixtures in packages/spec/test cover both directions.
title: AID Framework spec v0.1
description: The declarative source of truth for an AID application. Hand-authored against design doc §6, narrowed to the implemented surface (§14): the Phase 0 sections (models, prompts, tools, evals, pipelines) plus Phase 1 retrieval (stores, retrievers, the retrieve step and the retrieval metric). Top-level keys outside this set are rejected rather than ignored, so a feature that has not been implemented cannot be silently dropped. Within an implemented section, a sub-feature Phase 1 does not serve is rejected by a spec-local rule (`spec/not-supported`) rather than by the schema, so the enum stays the design doc's and the message can name the phase. See packages/spec/README.md for the scope boundary and the deferred keys.

specVersion.description: Spec language version. Only 0.1 exists; a different value is a hard error rather than a best-effort parse.

types.description: Named structured types referenced by prompts (structured output) and tools (input/output).

models.description: Model aliases. The alias is what the rest of the spec refers to; the vendor id is pinned here and only here.

stores.description: Vector store instances. `kind: memory` is the fully supported default and needs no service; `kind: pgvector` is declarable here and its adapter ships with the retrieval runtime.

retrievers.description: Retrievers: what to index, how to chunk it, which embedding model and store to use, and how to rank.

name.description: snake_case identifier for a spec node.

typeName.description: UpperCamelCase name of a declared type.

fieldType.description: A primitive (string, number, integer, boolean) or a declared type name, optionally suffixed with [] for a list.

namespace.description: Dotted namespace used to qualify generated symbols.

targets.description: Generator targets to emit. Defaults to [py-fastapi] when omitted.

kind.description: Only struct is in spec v0.1. enum/union/list land with the agents work, and adding them is a schema change, not a silent widening.

required.description: Defaults to false. Drives required-vs-optional on the generated side.

enum.$comment: A deliberate, minimal widening beyond the approved §3 sketch: structured output is the whole point of spec v0.1 and a classification field is the most common shape it takes. The minimum/maximum keys already establish that scalar constraints belong on a field.

provider.description: The Phase 0 provider set. `fake` is deterministic and keyless, which is what lets the eval gate run offline in CI.

modelId.description: Pinned vendor model id. Never an alias or a moving target: the resolved id is recorded in the IR so a run is reproducible.

capabilities.description: Declared model capabilities. json-schema is negotiated within a prompt (a structured-output prompt must bind a model that declares it) and embeddings within a retriever (a retriever's embedModel must declare it); the others are recorded in the IR for the capability gate to use in later phases.

fallbacks.description: Ordered model aliases to fail over to. Simple alias failover only; no routing policy in Phase 0.

costProfile.description: Name of a priced entry in the pinned model catalog. Omit to resolve it from the catalog by modelId.

baseUrl.description: Required for openai-compatible. Never a credential.

apiKeyEnv.$comment: The *name* of an environment variable, never a key. The pattern cannot express a literal secret, so a committed credential is out of scope by construction.

version.description: Bumped by hand when the template changes. The prompt identity includes it (prompt:<name>@<version>) so a revision does not move the IR node id.

template.description: Mustache-style text. Placeholders are {{variable}} references and are checked by the parser for well-formedness; whether each one resolves is a build-time IR gate, not a schema concern.

description.description: Shown to the model once model-selected tool choice exists (Phase 2). Required now so the field never has to be added retroactively.

sideEffects.description: Drives the fail-closed security gate: write and destructive require auth.

handler.description: Where the implementation lives. `business` means a user-owned module, so the generated code imports it rather than inlining logic.

auth.description: PolicyExpr source. Parsed once, on the TypeScript side, into a JSON AST that the runtime interprets; the string form never reaches a runtime.

kind.description: `memory` is the fully supported default and is what every gated test uses; `pgvector` is declarable in Phase 1 but no gate requires a database, so a pgvector-backed app is never the only thing that can pass.

uri.$comment: The pattern *is* the requirement: it cannot express a literal DSN, so a committed credential is out of scope by construction - the same trick `model.apiKeyEnv` uses. The security gate re-checks the resolved value, because the IR can carry a uri the schema never saw.

dimensions.description: Vector width. It must agree with the embedding model's own width; the normalize gate compares the two.

kind.description: Only `file` is implemented in Phase 1. s3/http/db/mcp are reserved by the design and rejected by a spec-local rule until the phase that ships their loaders, so a spec can be written against the final spelling without being silently ignored.

strategy.description: `semantic` is reserved: it needs an embedding pass over the whole source at ingest, which Phase 1 does not implement, so a spec-local rule rejects it.

size.description: Target chunk size in characters. The cost gate turns it into tokens at a fixed characters-per-token ratio, so estimates compare.

embedModel.description: Model alias that must declare the `embeddings` capability; the referential gate enforces that.

hybrid.description: Blend the lexical and the vector ranking instead of ranking on the vector alone. Off by default, so a retrieval that needs no lexical half declares nothing.

topK.description: Candidates the retriever returns per query. This is the retriever's value; Phase 1 has no step-level override.

model.description: Model alias the reranker is bound to. Phase 1 ships a deterministic lexical reranker, so the alias is a `fake` or local model; a hosted reranker adapter is a later phase's seam.

filters.description: Reserved: the expression form is not implemented in Phase 1, so a spec-local rule rejects it rather than accepting a filter nothing applies.

mode.description: `incremental` and `schedule` are reserved: an index that claims to refresh incrementally but is rebuilt from scratch is a lie, so a spec-local rule rejects both until the ingestion runtime honours them.

traits.description: Behavioural traits the generated retrieval path must honour. `citations` means retrieved items carry the source path and offsets a generated answer can cite.

target.description: Only pipelines are evaluable in Phase 0.

gate.description: How this eval's result is compared against the committed baseline. Never an equality check: sampling noise is expected, so the gate is a threshold on the regression relative to the baseline.

ci.description: When true this eval runs in the CI gate. At least one eval per HTTP-triggered pipeline should set it (an IR warning, not a schema rule).

maxRegression.description: Largest tolerated absolute drop in the metric's score versus the baseline.

samples.description: Runs per case. More samples shrink the sampling-uncertainty term the gate also requires before it fails.

kind.description: Allowed in the spec but rejected by a spec-local rule when gate.ci is true: a judging model is neither deterministic nor available offline, so it can never be part of the CI gate.
Deterministic and offline: it compares the ranking against known-correct source paths, so unlike llm-judge it is allowed under gate.ci.

expectDocs.description: Source paths, spelled relative to the retriever's source uri, that the ranking must place inside the top k. A warning in the eval-coverage gate if a spec declares retrievers and no eval measures them.

context.description: Binding name holding retrieved items: a retrieve step's result. The generator passes the items to the prompt and returns the citation list alongside the model call.

tool.description: Explicitly invoked by the pipeline, never chosen by the model. That is what keeps Phase 0 control flow plain async while still exercising the tool, auth and tracing seams.

retrieve.description: One retrieval over a declared retriever, bound to `as` for a later generate step's `context`. Retrieval is an explicit pipeline step rather than something a step does implicitly, so what was searched and in what order stays visible in the spec.

query.description: Mustache-style text, checked for well-formedness like a prompt template. A placeholder naming a later step's binding is a build-time IR error, not a schema one.

binding.description: Name a step's result is bound to for later steps.

stepInput.description: Flat map of scalars. A string may be a single {{path}} reference or a template containing several; nested values are deliberately out of scope for Phase 0.
